title: What Is Chatway MCP? A Plain-English Guide (2026)
summary: What is Chatway MCP? It's a connector for AI agents in Chatway inboxes, similar to automation tools. You'll understand its capabilities and what's missing.
body_markdown:
## Frequently asked questions


### Before you start


Where Chatway's pages are silent, the answer below says so; most of what you would verify comes down to five questions.


### Cost and compatibility


Is Chatway MCP free to use? Partly: Chatway's pages say MCP is included on every plan, including Free, and its conversations count toward the plan's conversation allowance. They don't publish any separate MCP fee, so whether one exists is an open question. Ask Chatway before budgeting around it.


Does Chatway MCP work with Claude or ChatGPT? Check the supported-client list on Chatway's MCP pages rather than assuming.


The pages document a set of clients and a set of tools, but a client missing from that list is unsupported until Chatway says otherwise. A Russian-language guide also exists, which helps if your team works in Russian.


### Safety and ownership


Is it safe to give an AI agent access to customer chats? Chatway hasn't published enough for me to call it safe. Agents act through the tools you expose, so treat every tool as a permission.


Start in a test workspace with the narrowest access, and look for documented limits on what the agent can read and send before connecting live conversations.


Who owns Chatway? The MCP pages I'm relying on don't answer this. Look at the company's terms, privacy policy, or legal page, which should name the contracting entity. You need that name for any data-processing agreement.


### What to do first


What should I check before trying Chatway MCP on Monday? Confirm your client is supported, then confirm that usage stays within your plan's conversation allowance. Ask in writing about MCP fees and data handling, and run one low-stakes task in a throwaway workspace first.
